questions.stem: The nurse leaves the room of a client with C. diff. Which hand hygiene is correct?

options.text: Gloves only, no hand hygiene needed

questions.explanation: B is correct: alcohol gel doesn't kill C. diff spores, so you scrub them off with soap and water. A and D rely on gel. C skips hand hygiene, which standard precautions require after every client.

questions.stem: A client is admitted with suspected tuberculosis. Which action is best?

options.text: Private room with the door open
Negative-pressure room and an N95 for staff

questions.explanation: B is correct: tuberculosis is airborne, so it needs a negative-pressure room and a fit-tested N95. A doesn't contain airborne particles. C, a surgical mask, isn't enough. D is contact precautions.

questions.stem: Which infections require airborne precautions? Select all that apply.
questions.explanation: A, B, and C are correct: tuberculosis, measles, and chickenpox spread in tiny floating particles. D, flu, is droplet. E, resistant staph, is contact.

questions.stem: A client on airborne precautions must go to radiology. What should the client wear during transport?
questions.explanation: B is correct: if the client has to leave the room, the client wears a regular surgical mask. A, the N95, is for staff. C is contact precautions. D leaves others unprotected.

questions.stem: A client has pertussis (whooping cough). Which precautions does the nurse use?

options.text: Droplet: surgical mask and private room

questions.explanation: B is correct: pertussis is a droplet infection, so a surgical mask and a private room are used. A is for airborne germs. C is for contact germs. D alone isn't enough for a droplet germ.

questions.stem: Which infections require contact precautions? Select all that apply.
questions.explanation: A, B, C, and D are correct: these spread by touch from skin or surfaces. E, measles, is airborne.

questions.stem: Which practice is part of contact precautions?

options.text: Keeping a dedicated stethoscope in the room
Keeping the door closed at all times

questions.explanation: A is correct: contact precautions use a gown, gloves, and dedicated equipment like a stethoscope that stays in the room. B, C, and D are airborne precautions.

questions.stem: In what order should the nurse put on personal protective equipment?
questions.explanation: B is correct: put on gown, mask, goggles, then gloves. A and D put gloves on early, so the gloves can't cover the gown cuffs and get dirty while you finish. C puts on gloves before the gown and leaves goggles last.

questions.stem: Which item should the nurse remove first when taking off personal protective equipment?
questions.explanation: C is correct: gloves are the dirtiest, so they come off first. The order is gloves, goggles, gown, then mask, all before leaving the room; only a respirator is removed after leaving the room and closing the door. A, the gown, B, the mask, and D, the goggles, come off after the gloves.

questions.stem: Which statement about standard precautions is correct?

options.text: They are used only for clients with known infections
They are used for every client
They are needed only when blood is visible

questions.explanation: B is correct: standard precautions are for every client because you can't tell who's carrying something. A and D limit them wrongly. C is wrong because hand hygiene is part of standard precautions.
